title: PAY-1: Stripe webhook retries can double-charge customers
content:
Issue PAY-1: Stripe webhook retries can double-charge customers
Type: Bug · Priority: Critical · Status: Done · Assignee: Sam Okafor · Labels: bug, payments, incident

When our webhook handler times out, Stripe retries `payment_intent.succeeded`. The handler is not idempotent, so a slow first attempt followed by a retry creates two ledger entries and sends two receipts.

**Fix direction:** store the Stripe event ID with a unique constraint and skip already-processed events.

title: Payments on-call runbook
content:
# Payments on-call runbook

## Duplicate charges

If a customer reports being charged twice, check `processed_stripe_events` for the Stripe event ID. A missing row means the webhook deduplication was bypassed; escalate to the payments lead. Refund the duplicate from the Stripe dashboard, never by editing the ledger.

## Reconciliation failures

The nightly reconciliation job runs at 01:00 UTC with a 30 minute limit. At month end volume triples. If it times out, rerun it for the failed date range with `recon run --from <date> --to <date>`; the batched version streams 10,000 transactions per page.

## Fraud-check 502s

The fraud-check service reloads its model nightly between 02:00 and 03:00 UTC. Checkout retries fraud-check once; if 502s exceed 1% page the risk team.

## Escalation

Page the payments lead through PagerDuty for anything affecting more than 10 customers or any data correction.

title: Authentication architecture
content:
# Authentication architecture

## Tokens

Access tokens are ES256 JWTs valid for 15 minutes. Refresh tokens rotate on every use and belong to a token family; reusing an old refresh token revokes the whole family.

## Password reset

Reset links contain a single-use token valid for 30 minutes. Only the SHA-256 hash of the token is stored. Requesting a reset never reveals whether the email exists.

## Login protection

Failed logins are counted per account and per IP in Redis. After five failures the delay grows exponentially. Passwords are hashed with argon2id and checked against known breached passwords.

## Deactivation

Deactivating a user must revoke every refresh token family and block new logins immediately.
